description: Optional host-native Linear tracker adapter layered on the run-delivery profile, whose commands run on POSIX hosts only. Review acquisition supports native subagents without Python helpers and exact content-based base-move reopening. Declared delivery-product gates, recovery and honest cost coverage remain host-native. Terminal handoffs retain the bound review release identity and any mid-review install. Shared v2 run observations retain selected structured output through compatible runtime capture. Coherent round briefs separate bounded delivery from unbounded planning; candidate checkouts and shared resources are isolated explicitly. Merge recovery preserves source occurrence time separately from observation, with unknown timing left unknown. Views show stage-specific recorded times and compact cross-repository pull request identities. Native runless review reports use bounded observational capture and candidate-bound shared cards. Originating closure details are collapsed by default in shared review cards. Ready and merge hooks receive an exact runner-derived single or batch check mode without changing admission. The line map gains a plan chapter from an optional delivery-plan/1 input: which criteria are proven, from the record and producer evidence, what changed since approval, and what needs the engineer. The plan chapter also shows how the plan was approved, from an optional planReview: one line for its review rounds and outcome, and a folded review track and cards; approvals marked blocking raise a flag until they are done. A binding may let the lead choose a candidate's checks from its diff, recorded per reviewed head and voided by a new head; the record, results, views and stats name the lead's choice and reason, and without the option the provider selects as before. Delivery records can hold lane ownership, current story assignments, and temporary flakes scoped to a base commit and check. Authorized base merges can retain an aligned review through hand-off. Integration-base setup records its target and uses the integration checkout for delivery. Record writers are pinned by applied archive digest and changed through a parked lead transition. Integration-base moves preserve recorded commit ancestry and recover publication and applied-writer reconciliation once. A stopped base rerun is told from a failed one, a named repair lands first and alone through a queue its broken base stopped, and a finish line that covers nothing is the lead's to mark. Follow-ups are filed only for findings still deferred, a round card says when an approval carried deferrable notes, and a delivery may declare that it defers nothing. A base move that changed nothing a check reads, by the binding's own declaration, carries that check, and deliveries that merge into one base on a machine share one merge slot. The line map labels a carried check, a flaky base run and a peer's merge. A failed full-health run whose failing tests pass alone is recorded as flaky where the binding declares the rerun, lead-suite runs the lead's suite in its own checkout of a commit, and deliveries on one base see each other and warn on files a peer claimed. A bounded data-only public snapshot reuses line-map payloads while excluding history, raw artifacts and local execution details. Optional owned hosted publishing collects coherent source cuts, reconciles fenced writer receipts and keeps credentials out of view data and children. Owned hosted publishing starts or adopts an independent generation-aware watcher, bounds terminal close publication to 30 seconds, retains pending terminal cuts for ten-minute retries and supports credential-free archive viewing with explicit archive retry. Path-bearing public prose carries a visible omission marker while raw uploaded paths and configured secrets remain invalid. Credential-free terminal notifications reach an existing owner independently of lifecycle-lock contention and preserve one deadline per finished cut. Hosted publishing is qualified from exact built archive bytes in two independently configured adopters; the separately deployed viewer and its dependencies are excluded from workflow archives.
